hook: A small silver locket that heals almost anything, made by feeding one well-known anomaly into another. The catch is in the word "total": the article is really about a cure you have to ration by the clock. It is short, so you can read it in a few minutes.
whyItMatters:
SCP-427 sits in a cluster of articles connected through SCP-914, the machine that refines whatever is placed inside it, and SCP-500, the cure-all pills. Seeing what the Foundation does with a by-product of those two tells you a lot about how it treats useful anomalies.

It is also a classic take on the old idea that a perfect remedy can go too far. Healing here does not stop at healthy; it keeps improving the body past the point of being human.
thingsToNotice:
Note the asterisk on the object class. The locket itself is rated as harmless, while what it can produce gets a far more serious class, and that split says something about how the Foundation labels risk.

The numbers climb in steps through the description, from minutes of a cold to percentages of resistance and strength. The closing judgment by Oversight lands differently once you have followed that progression, especially given who is expected to keep the logbook.

related.note: The refining machine the locket came out of.
The pills that went into the machine, and that the locket partly replaces.
